summary: Miami must keep Buffalo's explosive plays from piling up, because the Dolphins allow them on 9.4% of snaps while the Bills generate them more often than any team in the league. Khalil Shakir creates 4.4 yards of separation, second-best in the league, and Miami's pass defense ranks 22nd to slow him down. Our model puts Buffalo at 84%, below the market's 90%, and the rushing matchup adds the most points toward the Bills.

MIA.detail: Miami's defense ranks 26th in explosive play rate (9.4% allowed). Buffalo ranks 1st (10.1%).
Miami's defense ranks 28th in stuff rate (18% generated). Buffalo ranks 1st (15%).
Miami's defense ranks 22nd in EPA per dropback (+0.04 allowed). Buffalo ranks 6th (+0.16).

BUF.detail: Buffalo ranks 2nd in YAC over expected per catch (+0.5 yds). Miami's defense ranks 13th (-0.2 yds allowed).
Buffalo's defense ranks 9th in pressure rate (23% generated). Miami ranks 28th (23%).
Buffalo ranks 6th in EPA per designed run (-0.02). Miami's defense ranks 31st (-0.05 allowed).
